# requireNonNumberLike

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not convertible to a number.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonNumberLike() — Returns the value after checking that it is not convertible to a number. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonNumberLike<T>(value: T, message: string = "Expected a non-numeric value."): T;
```

A finite number, or a string that converts to one. `NaN`, the infinities and the empty string are excluded, which is what separates this from a bare `Number(value)`.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                  | Type     | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------------------------------------------- | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                    | `T`      | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-numeric value."` | `string` | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with convertible to a number excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                             |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------------ |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is convertible to a number. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonNumberLike(NaN); // => NaN
requireNonNumberLike(Infinity); // => Infinity
requireNonNumberLike(1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonNumberLike("1.5"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
